headline: Democrats sweep the U.S. midterms as Canada awaits its budget
summary: Democrats won both chambers of Congress, ending Republican control and raising questions about tariffs and the Iran war. In Canada, attention turned to Thursday’s federal budget, while GTA housing stayed soft.

top.headline: Democrats win House and Senate
top.what: Democrats took control of both chambers in the midterms, a broad rebuke of President Trump.
top.why: It changes who controls investigations, spending and tariff oversight from January.

top.headline: Iran war and oil prices swing on talks
top.what: Oil moved with hopes of an Iran breakthrough and limited U.S. strikes.
top.why: Energy prices feed straight into Ontario gas and shipping costs.

top.headline: Federal budget set for Thursday
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tables the budget Nov. 5 with an immigration levels update.
top.why: It sets taxes, spending and deficit direction for Canadians.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue
top.what: Talks continue as Democrats vow to push back on tariffs and Canadian industry hopes for relief.
top.why: Tariffs shape Ontario manufacturing jobs and prices.

top.headline: GTA home sales down 7.9% in October
top.what: TRREB reported 5,603 sales, down from a year earlier.
top.why: Prices and sales show how rates are affecting buyers.

top.headline: Ford rules out new Toronto funding deal
top.what: Ford said the province will not sign a new financial deal for Toronto.
top.why: City budgets, taxes and transit service depend on it.

top.headline: Ontario deficit swells to $16.9B
top.what: Tariffs delayed the province’s return to balance.
top.why: It affects provincial spending and services.
